mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate consistently compresses the discount rate for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a weakening consumer demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 6.5%), the labor market weakness signals reduced consumer spending and corporate profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1.0% over the past three months signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate profits and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines > 1.0% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of slow GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth < 1.5%), the weak economic expansion reduces corporate revenue outlook, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 annualized growth < 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%) and a restrictive monetary policy (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) signal an environment of rising real interest rates, which compresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy
failure_condition: The joint condition of CPIAUCSL > 5.0% and FEDFUNDS > 4.5% fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
